Sheet "Steps": the empty Formula workbook's steps, as it ships.
Sheet "Parameters"
  Excel Table "Parameters", A1:B2
    Headers: name | value
    Row 2:  | 
  D1: Parameters: the fixed values your formulas use, one row per value. Put its name under name and the value under value, such as tax_rate and 0.2 (a plain number, not 20%), then read it by name in a formula: XLOOKUP("tax_rate", Parameters[name], Parameters[value]). Leave the Table empty if no formula uses a fixed value. See step 6 on the Steps sheet.
Sheet "Keys"
  Excel Table "Keys", A1:B2
    Headers: table | key_columns
    Row 2:  | 
  D1: Keys: only for a Table where a value was typed over a formula. Add one row for that Table, however many values were typed over in it: the Table's name under table, and under key_columns the typed column or columns that tell its rows apart, separated by commas, such as job_runs with run_id, or sales with region, month. Copilot uses them to find the row a typed value belongs to. If no column tells the rows apart, leave the Table out. A Table with no value typed over a formula needs no row here. See step 10 on the Steps sheet.
Sheet "Runs"
  A1: run_id
  B1: job_id
  C1: status
  D1: duration_mins
  E1: avg_retry_secs
  F1: dt
  A2: 95
  B2: 1
  C2: SUCCESS
  D2: 12
  E2: 2
  F2: 2026-09-23

  B3: 2

Sheet "Pivot"
  PivotTable "PivotTable1", A3:C11
    Source: the range Runs!A1:F10, read as the Table it would be: run_id | job_id | status | duration_mins | avg_retry_secs | dt
    Rows: dt, status
    Columns: Values
    Value "Count of run_id": Count of run_id
    Value "Average of duration_mins": Average of duration_mins
    Totals shown: none
    Cells: each value cell, what Excel last stored in it, then the Value it shows and the Rows and Columns items it stands for:
      B4: empty (Count of run_id; Rows dt 2026-09-23)
      C4: empty (Average of duration_mins; Rows dt 2026-09-23)
      B5: 1 (Count of run_id; Rows dt 2026-09-23, status FAILED)
      C5: 30 (Average of duration_mins; Rows dt 2026-09-23, status FAILED)
      B6: 2 (Count of run_id; Rows dt 2026-09-23, status SUCCESS)
      C6: 15 (Average of duration_mins; Rows dt 2026-09-23, status SUCCESS)
      B7: 1 (Count of run_id; Rows dt 2026-09-23, status TEST)
      C7: 5 (Average of duration_mins; Rows dt 2026-09-23, status TEST)
      B8: 1 (Count of run_id; Rows dt 2026-09-23, status (blank))
      C8: 15 (Average of duration_mins; Rows dt 2026-09-23, status (blank))
      B9: empty (Count of run_id; Rows dt 2026-09-24)
      C9: empty (Average of duration_mins; Rows dt 2026-09-24)
      B10: 1 (Count of run_id; Rows dt 2026-09-24, status FAILED)
      C10: 20 (Average of duration_mins; Rows dt 2026-09-24, status FAILED)
      B11: 3 (Count of run_id; Rows dt 2026-09-24, status SUCCESS)
      C11: 26.66666666666667 (Average of duration_mins; Rows dt 2026-09-24, status SUCCESS)
Order, each piece after every piece it reads:
  1. Excel Table "Parameters"
  2. Excel Table "Keys"
  3. Range "Runs!A1:F10"
  4. PivotTable "PivotTable1", reads Range "Runs!A1:F10"
Each final's query reads the steps it needs as CTEs in this order, each CTE after every CTE it reads.
